browser_lab_package_provenance.scope: This browser lab is a standalone teaching approximation. Use the linked source for the project implementation.

materials.title: `normal`
materials.excerpt: Normal supply is the control case. No events occur; the utility supplies the requested 1,000 kW IT load through two 700 kW gross paths at 0.95 distribution efficiency.

materials.title: `path_maintenance`
materials.excerpt: Path maintenance removes Path A from 300 s through 900 s. Utility supply remains available, but the surviving 700 kW gross Path B cannot deliver the full 1,000 kW IT request after distribution losses.

materials.title: `shared_domain`
materials.excerpt: Shared-domain failure removes the shared-controls dependency from both distribution paths between 300 s and 900 s. The utility remains available upstream, but neither path can reach the IT load.

materials.title: Review spatial capacity and phased development
materials.excerpt: A rack count is not a facility plan. Equipment requires service space, replacement routes, structural capacity and coordinated boundaries through every construction phase. Use the manuscript’s historical operating account to practise reporting what was actually stated without turning different area descriptions into one misleading density metric.

materials.title: Reviewer-facing measurements
materials.excerpt: These measurements describe execution of the 0.4.0rc1 working build on one Windows machine on 23 September 2026. They are observations, not latency targets, physical controller speeds or a scalability claim. The raw files retain every sample and the environment. Ordinary background processes were not isolated.

materials.title: Trace protection zones and the full trip chain
materials.excerpt: Protection is not a green status field at one current. It is a chain from the actual fault through measurement, logic, DC supply and interruption. Use a declared inverse-time curve to learn how a calculation behaves, then inspect what that curve cannot establish about CT saturation, electrical zones or selectivity.

materials.title: Electrical continuity model
materials.excerpt: single_load_electrical_continuity_v1 is a reduced steady-state electrical flow model with discrete failures and a finite battery. It does not solve AC load flow, switching transients, protection coordination, harmonics, thermal behavior or workload queues. Its bounded topology is a synthetic experiment, not a certified redundant design.

materials.title: Expose shared control failures
materials.excerpt: Can a shared control fault defeat both power paths?

materials.title: Inspect grounding, distortion and control-power loops
materials.excerpt: Low resistance, low distortion and a nominal battery voltage each answer only a narrowly defined question. This lesson turns those single numbers into explicit boundaries. Follow the ground current, compare harmonic denominators, and include the return conductor in the trip circuit before drawing any conclusion about service.

materials.title: Same 375 kWh, different outage outcomes
materials.excerpt: The time of a demand peak changes what a battery must supply. Three 30-minute schedules below each request 375 kWh, average 750 kW, and reach the same 1,000 kW peak. They share a 100 kWh battery and the same ten-minute loss of utility and generator supply. One is served throughout; the other two have different amounts of unserved energy.

materials.title: Scenario catalog
materials.excerpt: Question: how do stored energy, generator startup and surviving paths change delivered IT power during an outage?

materials.title: Separate physical routes, optical budgets and fabric capacity
materials.excerpt: Two fibres are not automatically two independent services, and a low optical loss is not automatically an application pass. Separate the physical administration route from the logical fabric, then calculate a narrow loss budget and post-uplink-loss capacity. The lesson adds communications reasoning without pretending that the existing electrical simulator already models packets.

materials.title: Separate PUE from continuity
materials.excerpt: How does assumed PUE change annual energy for the same 50 MW IT load?

materials.title: Separate UPS power, battery energy and trip DC
materials.excerpt: The battery lesson already distinguishes reserve from ride-through. Now separate three further boundaries: AC output energy, delivered DC energy and nominal end-of-life storage. Then examine the protection DC circuit, where enough ampere-hours can coexist with insufficient voltage at the device that must operate.

materials.title: Track energy before the outage
materials.excerpt: Why does the 50 kWh case last longer when it can charge first?

materials.title: Battery ride-through notebook
materials.excerpt: battery-ride-through.ipynb is a deterministic first-run teaching example for the bundled generator_failure scenario. It derives the 100 kWh ride-through (307.8 s) and absolute depletion (607.8 s), then compares the charging-enabled and charging-disabled 50 kWh cases.

materials.title: Quickstart
materials.excerpt: Start here: predict the ride-through of a synthetic 1,000 kW (1 MW) IT load with 100 kWh of stored battery energy, run the case, and explain its energy ledger.

materials.title: Tutorials
materials.excerpt: Datacenter engineers can start with a short, reproducible continuity experiment: predict battery ride-through for a synthetic 1 MW IT load, run it, and explain the energy ledger. The browser defaults to 100 kWh stored energy; the 50 kWh challenge changes only the opening reserve.

materials.title: Watch and reproduce the 1 MW experiment
materials.excerpt: Open the current 1 MW experiment or view a still frame.

materials.title: `generator_failure`
materials.excerpt: Generator failure tests finite stored energy. Utility and generator are both unavailable from 300 s to 900 s, so the battery is the only available source until it depletes.

materials.title: `utility_loss`
materials.excerpt: Utility loss tests generator pickup. The utility is unavailable from 300 s through restoration at 900 s. The generator remains available and becomes ready after the declared 30 s start delay.

materials.title: Audit generator banks and usable fuel
materials.excerpt: The original startup lessons ask whether a generator becomes available in time. This lesson asks a different question: can the available bank carry the backed load at all? Follow a source claim through its real-power conversion, post-loss capacity and fuel ledger. A failed arithmetic claim should stay failed even when the combined installed nameplates look impressive.

materials.title: Audit the correction before releasing the design
materials.excerpt: The final lesson asks for a justified release decision, not the largest possible green score. Bring capacity, connectivity, protection, thermal behaviour, controls and evidence together. Then audit a proposed correction from the manuscript’s separate campus example: a remedy is another engineering assertion and must be recalculated.

materials.title: Browser demo
materials.excerpt: Start with the 1 MW guided experiment, open the 50 MW generator-failure preset in the advanced workspace, or follow the twelve continuity lessons. The first result uses the local JavaScript continuity engine. Verify against Python explicitly loads the reference Python engine when you want a second calculation.

Every field is required, unknown fields are rejected, and JSON object keys must be unique.

materials.title: Evidence packet calculation method
materials.excerpt: The builder creates two exact course variants and the existing path-maintenance preset. Course cases are reconstructed from the public course recipe rather than by changing a finished run. Their scenario JSON is passed through SiteScenario.from_dict, then to simulate_continuity. Each scenario has a stable input_sha256; filenames for its scenario, run, and reports include that digest.

materials.title: External review protocol
materials.excerpt: This protocol is for a bounded review of software behavior and reproducibility. It is not a facility acceptance test, protection study, equipment validation, certification exercise, uptime claim, cooling/workload study, or physical-control procedure.

materials.title: Independent reviewer receipt template
materials.excerpt: This is a blank worksheet. It records no completed review, reviewer, affiliation, endorsement, or result. Complete it only after the reviewer has performed the work and has chosen what identity information to disclose.

materials.title: Surviving-path capacity and finite-battery ride-through
materials.excerpt: Two continuity results answer the first engineering questions:

materials.title: Test capacity, paths and common dependencies
materials.excerpt: The existing lessons show how a surviving path or shared controller can govern electrical service. Now extend that intuition into a state matrix. Installed equipment, connected equipment and independently substitutable equipment are different sets. A spare counts only when it can reach the required load in the state being assessed.

materials.title: 50 MW aggregate AI-cluster continuity case
materials.excerpt: Question: when a synthetic 50 MW aggregate IT load loses utility and generator supply, how long does a 5 MWh battery reserve support the IT boundary?

materials.title: Build an evidence-controlled load ledger
materials.excerpt: Begin where the original course leaves off: not with a bigger battery, but with a more disciplined definition of demand. A facility total is meaningful only when every term belongs to the same boundary and operating condition. In this lesson, a 20 MW IT allocation becomes a traceable facility ledger, while a second example demonstrates why conflicting source values must remain visible.

materials.title: Build an integrated commissioning evidence loop
materials.excerpt: A completed component test answers a component question. Integrated continuity requires an initial state, expected sequence, instruments, acceptance criteria, stop conditions and recovery boundary that span the service chain. Compare two clocks, then examine the measurement boundary behind an apparently precise efficiency number.

materials.title: Coordinate liquid cooling and thermal ride-through
materials.excerpt: Battery minutes do not create cooling minutes. Start with the manuscript’s mixed-cooling rack, then move to a separately labelled facility thermal model. The visual goal is to make both heat paths and their shared rejection boundary visible, so that the learner never mistakes a liquid-cooled label for complete removal of room heat.

materials.title: Declare transformer and fault-current boundaries
materials.excerpt: A current value without its voltage, power base and network boundary is easy to misuse. This lesson builds a small equivalent circuit in layers, then shows how changing an assumption changes a fault-current screen. The purpose is to expose model limits before equipment selection, not to turn an attractive fault animation into a completed short-circuit study.

materials.title: Explore a power system, one assumption at a time
materials.excerpt: The browser course contains twelve interactive lessons for datacenter engineers learning power continuity. No installation or account is needed. Open the atlas for all four chapters, or follow Next lesson.

materials.title: Explore power continuity across facility profiles
materials.excerpt: Choose a facility, stress its supply, and trace what reaches the IT load. The energy workspace combines an interactive isometric campus, interval power flows, editable equipment limits, a complete event replay and reproducible reports.

materials.title: Release scope and reproducibility
materials.excerpt: Version 2.0.0 — Infrastructure Engineering extends the local teaching and research application to 24 lessons. It retains the canonical 1 MW guide, eighteen presets, four facility profiles, scenario import, demand-timeline editing, sensitivity tools, reports, printable legacy worksheets, EMT and five power-dynamics studies. Twelve infrastructure lessons add bounded educational screens, se…

materials.title: Reproduction evidence
materials.excerpt: The 2.0.0 continuity engine remains a synthetic teaching model for one aggregate IT load. It covers utility/generator availability, finite battery energy, conversion losses, distribution-path limits, deterministic restoration, and interval energy accounting.
